scope: Theorem 8.1 (Adjoint positivity) of the manuscript “Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Projective-Hodge-lines-and-ordinary-Iitaka-subadditivity-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 564a98c625b94ef4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let P be a smooth connected projective complex variety and D a reduced simple normal crossing divisor. Let V be a rationally polarized integral pure variation on P \ D whose highest nonzero Hodge filtration piece is a line, and let L ∈ Pic(P) ⊗ Q be its rational parabolic extension. There are a projective birational morphism π : e P → P, with e P smooth, a smooth projective variety Z, a surjective morphism h : e P → Z with connected fibers, and a nef rational divisor A on Z such that π∗ L ∼Q h∗ A, KZ + aA is big for every sufficiently large rational a. Here a divisor on a point is big. Further smooth birational modifications of the source are per- mitted by replacing h with its composition with the modification.
